claim: Let \(S_2\) be Schemmel's second totient. Every composite integer \(n\) satisfying \(S_2(n)\mid\varphi(n)-1\) has at least \(617427\) distinct prime factors: \(\omega(n)\ge617427\). The proof combines the forced residue patterns modulo \(3\) with a modulo-\(5\) incompatibility in the only low-multiplier branches and exact integer interval certificates for the resulting extremal prime products. No existence of a Deaconescu number is asserted.
integrity: The symbolic reduction is proved in RESULT.md. The finite inequalities are certified by outward-rounded integer interval arithmetic in verify.py; no floating-point comparison is used for acceptance.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is a necessary lower bound only; it neither proves existence nor settles Deaconescu's conjecture. The cutoff is specific to the stated modulo-3/modulo-5 extremal-product sieve.
title: A 617,427-prime-factor lower bound for Deaconescu numbers
